name: Bakeries, mithai and confectionery

problems.words: Bread and buns left over every night, we sell them as rusk but it's a loss
quick_ideas: Note what's left at closing by item for a week, so production follows real sales
Bake the slow items in smaller batches through the day, because one big morning bake is where leftovers come from.

workzap_build.text: a leftover log by item and branch with what was reworked, discounted or discarded, feeding a daily production suggestion automatically.

problems.ask_first: Who decides how much to bake each day?
problems.free_stops: How the daily production plan is worked out by day and season goes in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: For one week, count leftover bread and buns by item at closing, so the biggest nightly loss stands out.
Give one person the closing job of writing leftovers in one notebook, so tomorrow's bake is based on yesterday's reality.

problems.words: Eid boxes run out at some branches while others have too many
quick_ideas: Pull last Eid's sales by branch from the register, so this year's split starts from evidence
Agree one person who can move boxes between branches during Eid, so surplus reaches the shortfall quickly.

workzap_build.text: factory-to-branch dispatch and receiving on phone, with live stock per branch and alerts when one runs low while another is full.

problems.ask_first: Is last year's Eid sale written down by branch anywhere?
problems.free_stops: The festival allocation method and transfer rules stay for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: During Eid week, compare boxes sent and boxes left unsold by branch each night, so uneven allocation is easier to spot.
Give one person the branch transfer list and evening check call, so extra Eid boxes move before the next rush.

problems.words: Factory sends to branches on a paper chit and nothing matches
quick_ideas: Have each branch count and sign what arrives, so gaps are caught on the day
Keep a copy of every chit at the factory, so both sides have the same record.

workzap_build.text: Dispatch and receiving would be recorded on phones, and any difference between factory and branch would be flagged to you every day.

problems.ask_first: Who checks the goods when they reach the branch?
problems.free_stops: The dispatch-to-receipt flow and variance rules are detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: For one week, compare each factory paper chit with what branches say arrived, so the mismatch point shows up clearly.
Give one branch person the arrival count and chit signoff duty, so shortages are raised while the same delivery is still fresh.

problems.words: Ghee, sugar and khoya prices change weekly, and I don't know which sweet makes money
quick_ideas: Cost your top sweets per kilo once from this week's bills, so you see which kilo rate is out of date
Review the kilo rate on the thinnest items first.

workzap_build.text: recipe costing per kilo that updates with every ingredient price change and flags sweets below your margin.

problems.ask_first: When did you last update the kilo rate?
problems.free_stops: The per-kilo costing method and rate review rules go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Pick a few top sweets and note this week's ingredient spending beside their selling rate, so weak earners stand out sooner.
Give one person a fixed weekly time to note changing ghee, sugar and khoya costs, so price decisions follow current buying reality.

problems.words: Custom cake orders come by WhatsApp, Instagram and phone — wrong names on cakes, and some not ready on time
quick_ideas: Write every custom order on one order form with design, message, date and time, so the kitchen works from one sheet
Read the cake message back to the customer before confirming, because most mistakes happen at intake.

workzap_build.text: Each custom cake order would be captured with design photo, message, pickup time and advance paid, kitchen tickets would be printed, and the customer would get a WhatsApp confirmation.

problems.ask_first: What usually goes wrong — design, timing or details?
problems.free_stops: The order flow from intake to pickup and the confirmation steps are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: For one week, count custom orders that needed name or timing corrections, so the intake mistakes are sized clearly.
Give one person one notebook for every custom cake order from all channels, so kitchen work follows the same details each time.

problems.words: Advance payments for cake orders are noted on paper and get lost
quick_ideas: Give every advance a receipt with an order number, so each payment ties to one order
Check advances against open orders at closing, so a missing one is caught the same day.

workzap_build.text: an advance-payment ledger tied to each order, matched daily with cash collected per branch.

problems.ask_first: Have advances actually gone missing, or just been hard to trace?
problems.free_stops: How advances, balances and daily closing are linked is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: At closing for one week, compare cake advances noted with open orders still pending, so missing payments are easier to catch.
Give one person the job of keeping all cake advances in one receipt book, so each payment stays tied to its order.

problems.words: Corporate Eid orders — offices pay months late
quick_ideas: List every corporate customer with what they owe and since when, so you know who to chase first
Agree payment terms in writing before the next festival order, so expectations are clear.

workzap_build.text: corporate order and receivables tracking with balances by customer label and automatic payment reminders.

problems.ask_first: How many corporate customers buy on credit?
problems.free_stops: The reminder schedule and credit rules per customer stay for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each corporate Eid order beside when payment actually arrived, so the slowest paying accounts become obvious.
Give one person one notebook for all corporate dues and follow ups, so collection calls happen from one current list.

problems.words: Karigars leave just before the festival, and the production plan is in the head karigar's head
quick_ideas: Write down the main recipes and daily quantities with the head karigar, so the business doesn't depend on one person
Talk to karigars before the festival about pay and overtime, so it isn't negotiated under pressure.

workzap_build.text: a daily production plan by product and branch with sign-off by the head karigar, and a festival planner with last year's volumes, staffing and boxes.

problems.free_stops: The production plan structure and festival planner are detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Watch one full production day and note which tasks only the head karigar decides, so the risky dependency is clearer.
Give one senior worker the job of writing daily quantities and sequence in one notebook, so festival production survives sudden absences.

problems.words: We don't take online orders, people message and leave
quick_ideas: Reply to every order message within the hour, because people move on fast
Share a simple menu with prices on WhatsApp and Instagram, so fewer people need to ask.

workzap_build.text: an online ordering page with pre-order slots for festivals, feeding the same order list as the shop.

problems.ask_first: Do you deliver, or do customers collect?
problems.free_stops: The ordering page design and slot rules are covered in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: For one week, count message enquiries that got no reply by closing, so missed online demand is easier to judge.
Give one person a fixed time to check and answer order messages, so interested buyers are not left waiting.

problems.words: Shop sales and factory costs are in different registers
quick_ideas: Bring each branch's daily sales into one sheet, so you see the business as a whole
Compare sales with factory purchases weekly, so a gap shows early.

workzap_build.text: a short morning read of every branch's sales and product mix alongside factory output, with the one thing to look at.

problems.ask_first: How do you see daily sales across branches now?
problems.free_stops: How shop and factory numbers are joined up goes in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: For one week, note daily branch sales beside factory spending in one notebook, so the rough mismatch is visible together.
Give one person the job of collecting both registers every evening into one notebook, so reviews stop waiting for missing pages.

never_say: Anything about shelf life, preservatives, colours, labelling or food-safety rules.
Allergen or diabetic-suitability claims for any product.
Employment-law advice on karigar pay disputes.
Help with fake halal or quality certificates, short weight, or under-invoicing corporate gift boxes.
That a festival plan will sell out or cut waste by any amount.

sample_reply.person: Eid pe har saal kuch branches mein dabbe khatam aur kuch mein bach jate hain. Koi hal batao.
sample_reply.pi: Ji haan, is ka hal mumkin hai, aur kaam is Eid se pehle shuru ho sakta hai. 1) Pichli Eid ki branch-wise sale register se nikal lein, taake is saal ka batwara andaze ke bajaye record par ho. 2) Eid ke dauran ek banda tay karein jo branches ke beech dabbe bhej sake, taake jahan bach rahe hain wahan se kami wali branch tak jaldi pohanchein. Workzap ye aap ke liye automatically kar sakta hai: factory se har branch ki dispatch aur receiving phone par, har branch ka live stock, aur jab ek branch mein kami aur doosri mein zyada ho to foran alert. Kya main aap ke liye solution document aur quote banwa doon? Mana bhi kar sakte hain.
